title: A Little Reminder as We Move Into a New Season
desc: A two minute fall reminder from Hallie on slowing down, noticing small beauty, and filling your mind with things that help you grow.
summary: Seasons change, and so do we. In this short fall episode, Hallie talks about how much is shifting right now, from the weather to the way she sees her own life, and why she is choosing to slow down instead of rushing through it.
It is a quick, gentle reset: a reminder to work through what you are carrying, notice the good things you might have walked past before, and keep feeding your mind with what actually helps you grow.
takeaways: Change is a normal part of every season of life
Slowing down helps you notice what you used to overlook
What you put into your mind shapes how you grow
reflect: What is one small, good thing you have been walking past without noticing?

title: You're Allowed to Want Something Different
desc: Hallie introduces My Inner Mind, the next chapter of My Sister's Closet, and asks what you have outgrown but not admitted to yourself yet.
summary: This is the official start of My Inner Mind. If you have been listening since the beginning, you know this show as My Sister's Closet. That chapter is not disappearing. It is becoming one part of something bigger, with room to talk about more than relationships and dating.

Hallie explains why the podcast needed to grow and what is coming next: loneliness, friendship, starting over, confidence, money, feeling stuck, learning to be alone, and letting people in. She also shares what she has been building behind the scenes, including the My Inner Mind app, Set It Down walks, community events, and a place where listeners can actually connect with each other.
The big question to take with you: what have you outgrown that you have not admitted to yourself yet?
takeaways: Changing your mind about your life is allowed
Outgrowing something is not the same as failing at it
Connection works better in community than through a microphone alone
reflect: What have you outgrown that you haven't admitted to yourself yet?

title: What Real Sisterhood Actually Looks Like: Safety, Honesty, Accountability, and Celebration
desc: The four things healthy friendship is built on: safety, honesty, accountability, and celebration, with research on co-regulation and capitalization.
summary: After four episodes on what sisterhood is not, Hallie flips the question. What does a healthy, close friendship actually look like, and how do you practice it?

She lands on four pillars. Safety, with research on co-regulation and how close relationships calm the nervous system. Honesty, and why repair matters more than never fighting. Accountability that goes both ways, illustrated by a twenty year friendship built on quick apologies. And celebration, with the psychology of capitalization: how someone responds to your good news says a lot about the relationship.
Real stories from Reddit about what healthy friendship feels like round it out. This is the payoff episode of the series.
takeaways: Good friendship is something you practice, not just the absence of drama
Feeling safe with someone can literally calm your body
How a friend reacts to your wins matters as much as how they show up in hard times
Repair is a two person job
reflect: Which is hardest for you to practice: safety, honesty, accountability, or celebration?
topics: how to be a good friend

What a healthy friendship feels like
How one friendship lasted over 20 years

Having someone to share good news with

title: Boundaries Without Honesty Become Walls: What Real Honesty in Friendship Looks Like
desc: Boundaries without honesty become walls. Honesty without boundaries becomes cruelty. Why healthy friendships need both.
summary: A boundary you never explain can quietly end a friendship instead of protecting it. And honesty with no boundaries can turn into cruelty. In part four of the series, Hallie looks at why healthy relationships need both at the same time.

She shares two people's answers to the question of what sisterhood means, walks through research on relational aggression, and reacts to a Reddit story about a friend whose brutal honesty always showed up at the worst possible moment. Brené Brown's research on vulnerability ties it together.
takeaways: An unexplained boundary can feel like a wall to the other person
Honesty needs care and timing to land as love
Vulnerability is what turns honesty into connection
reflect: Have you ever held a boundary without explaining it? What happened to that friendship?
topics: how to set boundaries without cutting people off

chapters.title: What one woman said sisterhood means
What research says about indirect conflict

What a healthy connection looks like

title: Silent Treatment, Scorekeeping, and Loyalty Tests: The Hidden Ways We Fight in Friendships
desc: Not every fight looks like a fight. The silent treatment, scorekeeping, and loyalty tests, and what to say out loud instead.
summary: Some of the most painful conflicts never include a single raised voice. In part three, Hallie breaks down three sideways ways people fight in friendships instead of speaking up directly.

She separates silence used to calm yourself down from silence used as punishment, reacts to a Reddit story about a two week silent treatment over a small disagreement, and explains how scorekeeping turns a simple conversation into a courtroom. She also looks at loyalty tests, where someone pressures you to pick sides, and how that differs from noticing real exclusion.
takeaways: Taking space to calm down is healthy; going silent to punish is not
Keeping score turns friends into opponents
Loyalty tests force people to choose instead of talk
Saying the thing out loud is usually kinder than performing it
reflect: What have you been fighting without actually fighting it? What do you need to say out loud instead?

chapters.title: Not every fight looks like a fight
When every argument becomes a courtroom
What have you been fighting without fighting?

title: When Therapy Speak Becomes a Weapon: Emotional Intelligence Gone Wrong in Friendships
desc: When therapy speak shuts conversations down instead of opening them up. Tone policing, deflection, and what real emotional safety looks like.
summary: Emotional intelligence is supposed to bring people closer. But phrases borrowed from therapy can also be used to end a conversation before the real issue ever gets addressed.

Hallie looks at the difference between healthy communication and weaponized therapy speak, like refusing to engage because of someone's tone or telling them they are projecting. She reacts to a Reddit story that split commenters down the middle, talks about the line between regulating yourself and controlling someone else, and shares a personal time she was told her tone was the problem.
takeaways: Healthy language can be misused to avoid accountability
Regulating yourself is different from controlling the other person
Focusing only on tone can be a way to dodge the actual issue
reflect: Has someone ever used your tone to avoid the actual issue? How did you handle it?

title: Why Do Friends Ghost Each Other? The Real Reasons Behind Friendship Ghosting
desc: Why people ghost their friends, what it feels like on the receiving end, and the patterns that make disappearing feel safer than speaking up.
summary: Ghosting is not just a dating problem. In the first episode of The Other Side of Sisterhood, Hallie looks at why people disappear from friendships, and why it is rarely about cruelty.

She walks through the cycle of deflection and dismissed feelings that can make silence feel like the only option, talks honestly about what it feels like to be the one left behind, and reacts to a Reddit story about someone who ghosted her best friend of seven years.
takeaways: People usually ghost because speaking up stopped feeling safe
Repeated dismissal can slowly push someone toward silence
Being ghosted hurts, and it is still worth looking for the patterns
reflect: At what point did disappearing from a friendship feel safer than speaking up?

title: What Failure Taught Me (And Why I'm Not Afraid of It Anymore)
desc: Hallie shares the event almost nobody came to, what she believed about herself afterward, and how failure became one of her best teachers.
summary: Hallie once planned an event that almost no one attended. At the time, it felt like proof she was not capable. Looking back, it taught her more than almost anything else.

In this episode she talks about why failure feels so personal, choosing to try again, whether you are playing it too safe, and redefining failure after divorce and broken expectations. She also covers giving yourself grace, the danger of assuming what others think, and why this might finally be a winning season.
takeaways: Failure feels personal, but it is information, not identity
Playing it safe has a cost too
Grace makes it possible to try again
Many of our fears are built on assumptions
reflect: What is one failure that taught you something you'll never forget?

title: When Life Starts Making Sense Again
desc: A short, hopeful check-in on what it feels like when the dots finally connect, plus why your perspective is never the only one.
summary: A short and sweet one. Hallie stops by to share a good day: her health, her vision, and her creative direction are starting to connect, and for the first time in a while she can see the road ahead.

She also shares an idea from 101 Essays That Will Change the Way You Think about naive realism, the habit of assuming everyone sees the world the way we do, and why remembering that your view is just one view can change how you show up for people.
takeaways: Clarity often arrives slowly, then all at once
We tend to assume others see what we see
Your perspective is real, and it is not the only one
reflect: Where in your life are the dots starting to connect?

title: Slowing Down to Speed Up
desc: Six months in, Hallie talks giver burnout, practicing what you preach, and why she took July off to actually live the life she talks about.
summary: Six months into the podcast, Hallie gets honest about where she is. She came across the term giver burnout and recognized herself in it, which led to a hard question: is she actually living the intentional life she talks about, or just talking about it?

She explains why she stepped away for the month of July, not because she was done, but to rest and live what she has been teaching. She also talks about measuring a good life by presence instead of production, and previews the August series and conversations that include everyone, not just sisters.
takeaways: Givers burn out too, often quietly
Rest is part of the work, not a break from it
A good life is measured by presence, not output
reflect: Are you living the life you talk about, or just talking about it?

Taking a Christmas in July break
This was never just about sisterhood

title: The Other Side of Adoption
desc: The parts of adoption people don't talk about: returned kids, harmful homes, and the thousands who age out of foster care every year.
summary: Adoption is not always the fairy tale it is made out to be. Closing out her adoption conversations for now, Hallie gets honest about the hard parts: children who get returned, homes that are worse than where kids came from, and the thousands of young people who age out of foster care each year with nowhere to go.

She shares difficult statistics, a story that has stayed with her since high school, and what it feels like to be placed into a life you did not choose. It is a heavy episode, and an important one for adoptees, foster youth, and anyone who loves them. Resource mentioned: Second Shift Birmingham.
takeaways: Adoption can hold both love and loss
Aging out of foster care leaves many young adults without support
Adoptees deserve space to tell the whole story
reflect: What do you wish more people understood about adoption or foster care?

title: Being Other: My Story on Adoption, Race, and Never Fitting the Mold
desc: Growing up adopted, biracial, homeschooled, and a preacher's kid. Hallie on never fitting one box, and why being other became a gift.
summary: Hallie goes deeper into her story: growing up biracial in a big blended family, homeschooled, a preacher's kid, with a stutter, and constantly asked who her real parents were.

She shares hard memories, including being asked to leave rooms so others could tell racist jokes, a moment on a mission trip where she finally felt like she belonged, and what her siblings taught her about not changing who you are to fit in. If you have ever felt like the chameleon in the room, this one is for you.
takeaways: Shapeshifting to fit in has a cost
Belonging can show up in unexpected places
Being different can become a strength
reflect: Where have you changed yourself just to fit in?

title: My Adoption Story
desc: Adopted at three months old into a family of eight kids, Hallie shares her adoption story: belonging, being other, and what family means.
summary: Hallie shares something she had never fully talked about on the show: her adoption story. She joined her family at three months old, the fourth of what became eight kids. None of them were biological siblings, none of them looked alike, and all of them were family.

She talks about growing up biracial in a mostly white Christian home, the questions strangers asked out loud, feeling like the other in every room, her brother with fetal alcohol syndrome, and the words her dad said to the caseworker that still mean everything to her. It is warm, funny in places, and deeply personal.
takeaways: Family is built, not just born
Being different can be okay, even good
The stories our parents tell us about ourselves stay with us
reflect: What does family mean to you, beyond biology?

title: Silence Is the Call for Help
desc: When a friend goes quiet, it isn't always because things are fine. Why sharing your struggles is trust, not burden.
summary: Hallie comes straight from Pilates with a friend of twenty years who had gone quiet. Not because things were fine, but because she did not want to be a burden.

This episode is about why silence is not protection, the difference between burdening someone and trusting them, and three things Hallie came home thinking about: share, hold, and replenish. She also opens up about a tattoo, a hard season in college, and the friend who showed up for her then.
takeaways: Hiding your struggles hurts the people who love you too
Letting someone in is an act of trust
Your quiet friends may need a check-in most
reflect: Who in your life has gone quiet lately? Who could you let in?

title: The Refreshing Period (A Follow Up)
desc: A short follow up on what the refreshing period looks like in practice: space to grow, room to understand, and choosing joy together.
summary: A quick but important follow up. Hallie clarifies what the refreshing period looks like in real life: giving each other space to grow, letting misunderstandings turn into understanding, and choosing to share joy instead of holding on to pain.
She also shares learning something shocking about someone she considers a sister, and how they chose to move forward anyway. This closes the react, reflect, repair, refresh arc.
takeaways: A fresh start needs room for both people to grow
Understanding often comes after the misunderstanding
Moving forward is a choice you make together
reflect: Is there a relationship that needs a fresh start more than another conversation?

title: The Refreshing Period and What Sisterhood Really Means
desc: After the reaction, reflection, and repair comes the refresh. Starting from a clean slate and what close relationships look like after they're tested.
summary: After the reaction, the reflection, and the repair, what comes next? Hallie finally gets to the refreshing period: starting from a clean slate, giving people space, and showing up differently going forward.

She also talks about what sisterhood means to her as one of four adopted daughters in a family of eight, how buried memories surfaced mid-conversation, why trauma affects everyone around you, forgiving without forgetting, saying hard things out loud, and the difference between sitting with people in pain and standing with them in joy. Mentioned: The Body Keeps the Score.
takeaways: Repair is not the end; the refresh is where trust rebuilds
Forgiving without forgetting can be healthy
Hard things need to be said out loud
Showing up in joy matters as much as in pain
reflect: Who do you show up for in hard times but forget to celebrate with?

chapters.title: Working to understand each other better
Sisters who've fought for each other

title: What's Actually Motivating You
desc: Intrinsic vs extrinsic motivation, the detour Hallie took from her original plan, and why meaning is something you assign, not find.
summary: If the last two episodes cracked something open, this one asks what you are going to do with it. Hallie digs into a chapter from 101 Essays That Will Change the Way You Think about intrinsic motivation: being driven from the inside instead of chasing approval.

She talks about the gap between who she thought she would become and what she is building now, why meaning is something you give your life rather than something you stumble on, and shares an early look at the journaling and community app she was building.
takeaways: Motivation that comes from inside lasts longer
Detours can lead you somewhere better
You assign meaning; you don't just find it
reflect: If no one ever saw it, would you still do what you're doing?

title: Feeling Triggered? How to Repair When You Know Better
desc: What happens when you know better but don't do better? Hallie on getting triggered, real apologies, and what repair actually looks like.
summary: Hallie had a moment that put her own advice to the test, and she did not pass. This episode is about what she did next.

She walks through what she was feeling and why, the limits of playing devil's advocate, the difference between an apology that changes things and one that doesn't, and what the repair actually looked like.
takeaways: Knowing better doesn't mean you'll always do better
A real apology comes with a change
Repair is possible after you mess up
reflect: What does a real apology look like to you?

title: It Starts Inside: Reflection, Wellness, and Sisterhood
desc: A check-in from the car on flow states, creativity, and what the foundations of close relationships actually require.
summary: A quick, unfiltered check-in. A chapter from 101 Essays That Will Change the Way You Think on Zen, flow states, and creativity stopped Hallie in her tracks because it connects directly to what she is building with My Inner Mind.
A listener also asked about the foundations of sisterhood, and Hallie gets real about what that requires, including a disagreement with her own sisters she is still working through.
takeaways: Flow and creativity start with an inner reset
Close relationships require ongoing work
Disagreement doesn't have to mean disconnection
reflect: When was the last time you felt fully in flow?

title: The Sunday Slow Down
desc: A simple three step reset for busy people: one journal sentence, five minutes of stretching, and a shower. Plus the first look at Set It Down Saturdays.
summary: Hallie had twenty free minutes on a Sunday and did what builders always do: made something. But this episode is about the opposite. It is about stopping, resting, and filling yourself back up before you run empty.

She shares her big three for slowing down when life won't: one sentence in your journal, five minutes of stretching, and a shower, all in thirty minutes or less. She also talks about finding joy in chores and gives a first look at Set It Down Saturdays.
takeaways: Rest can be small and still count
One sentence, five minutes of stretching, and a shower is enough to reset
You can't pour into others from an empty cup
reflect: What would your own big three for slowing down be?

title: Let's Talk Depression: What Your Mind Is Really Trying to Tell You
desc: Hallie gets honest about living with depression: masking, high-functioning depression, and how creativity and connection helped.
summary: Hallie opens up about something she has carried most of her life: depression. From therapy as a teenager to medication, masking pain, and the long road of figuring out what actually helps, this is an honest and necessary conversation.

She talks about the basics her therapists always came back to (eat, sleep, exercise), why they matter but are not the whole picture, and how creativity and connection have been just as healing. She also shares what she wishes she had known sooner about EMDR and somatic movement, and what high-functioning depression feels like when you keep pushing through.
takeaways: Eating, sleeping, and moving help, but they aren't everything
Masking pain can look like doing fine
Creativity and connection can be part of healing
Small moments of connection matter more than we think
reflect: What small thing helps you feel a little more like yourself on a hard day?

title: When Siblings Make It About Themselves: Wedding Drama Reaction
desc: A sister wants to announce her pregnancy at the bride's wedding. Hallie reacts and unpacks boundaries, communication, and sibling dynamics.
summary: On this Sunday Fun Day episode, Hallie reacts to a story that spirals fast: a bride is getting ready for her wedding when her sister asks to announce her pregnancy during the celebration.

Hallie unpacks what happens when family members can't clearly name or say what they feel, and talks about boundaries, communication, and why sibling dynamics get so complicated around big life moments.
takeaways: Big moments bring old family dynamics to the surface
Unspoken feelings tend to come out sideways
Clear boundaries protect important days
reflect: How do you handle it when someone else's moment brings up your own feelings?

title: AITA Sunday React: Who's Really in the Wrong?
desc: Hallie reacts to Am I the Jerk style Reddit stories, breaks down the drama, and asks you to decide who's really in the wrong.
summary: A lighter Sunday episode. Hallie reacts to some of the latest Am I the A-hole stories from Reddit, breaking down the drama, the awkward moments, and the twists nobody saw coming.
Along the way she looks at what each person might have been feeling and what could have gone differently. Listen in and decide for yourself who was really in the wrong.
takeaways: Most conflicts have more than one side
How something is said matters as much as what is said
It's easier to see patterns in other people's stories first
reflect: When was the last time you weren't sure if you were the one in the wrong?

title: Resilience, Redefined
desc: What if resilience isn't always holding on? Knowing when to keep going, when to let go, and why self-honesty is the real strength.
summary: We are often taught that strength means holding on, quitting is weakness, and pushing through is the only way forward. But what if resilience looks different than that?

This episode sits with a hard question: how do you know when to keep going and when letting go is the brave choice? Hallie reframes resilience as self-honesty rather than willpower, and talks about recognizing what no longer serves you and choosing yourself anyway.
takeaways: Endurance and strength are not the same thing
Letting go can be the brave choice
Resilience starts with being honest with yourself
reflect: What are you holding on to just to prove you can?

title: Meet Micah: Fun, Real, and Full of Life
desc: Hallie's sister Micah joins for five fun questions, everyday habits that keep her mindset steady, and an honest talk about resilience.
summary: Hallie sits down with her sister Micah for a conversation that feels like listening in on a real sibling chat. It starts with five fun questions so you can get to know Micah beyond being Hallie's sister.

Then it gets practical. Micah shares the simple, everyday things she does to brighten her day and keep her mindset in a good place. They close on resilience: what it really looks like when you are a spouse, a parent, and someone with a very full plate.
takeaways: Small daily habits can protect your mindset
Resilience looks like showing up even on hard days
A full life can still be a well-tended one
reflect: What is one small habit that reliably makes your day better?

title: Saturday Reflection: Is Procrastination Really About Avoiding Decisions?
desc: Is procrastination about avoiding work, or avoiding decisions? A Saturday reflection on emotional avoidance, needing space, and grief.
summary: Hallie takes a slow Saturday pause to ask whether procrastination is really about avoiding work, or about avoiding decisions.

She explores emotional avoidance, what people really mean when they say they need space, how grief can show up in unexpected ways, and why slowing down can be one of the most productive things you do. Ideas from 101 Essays That Will Change the Way You Think run through the conversation.
takeaways: Procrastination is often a decision you haven't made yet
Needing space can mean many different things
Slowing down can move you forward
reflect: What decision have you been avoiding by staying busy?

summary: Hallie and her sister Libby react to a viral Reddit story about a first date gone wrong, and it opens up a bigger conversation about dating.

takeaways: Activity dates take the pressure off
Have a safe exit plan for any first date
An honest no is usually kinder than ghosting

title: Testing the Mic, Finding Myself
desc: Recorded live at Libby's house: on identity beyond your past, self-awareness, and why life gets easier as you grow wiser.
summary: Recorded live at her sister Libby's house, this episode is about who you are beyond what has happened to you.

Hallie draws on two essays from 101 Essays That Will Change the Way You Think to talk about self-awareness, identity, and the idea that life doesn't necessarily get easier, you just get wiser about how to handle it.
takeaways: You are more than your past experiences
Self-awareness is a skill you can grow
Growth often looks like handling the same things better

title: Making a Risky Turn: Reflections in the Luteal Phase
desc: A drive-and-talk bonus episode on hormones, seasonal low moods, breaking old patterns, and why emotions need a way out.
summary: A bonus episode recorded on the drive to her sister's house. Hallie was in her luteal phase, dealing with seasonal low moods, and under a full moon all at once, and used the moment to look at old patterns and decide what to keep.

She talks about hormonal emotional shifts, regulation, breaking patterns, the healing power of connection, and self-care as a daily practice, comparing unprocessed emotions to a volcano that needs somewhere to go. It also sets up her conversation with Libby about empathy.
takeaways: Hormones and seasons can amplify emotions
Unprocessed feelings build pressure
Daily self-care helps you notice patterns
reflect: Which old pattern are you ready to stop carrying?

title: Empathy in Action: Turning Reflection Into Repair
desc: The four qualities of empathy, why empathy means feeling with someone instead of fixing them, and how better listening builds connection.
summary: Continuing the emotional intelligence series, Hallie moves to empathy, which comes after self-awareness and self-regulation.

She explains Theresa Wiseman's four qualities of empathy: taking someone's perspective, staying out of judgment, recognizing their emotions, and communicating that you understand. The big idea is that empathy means feeling with someone, not fixing them. There is also a spa day update featuring a very uncooperative locker.
takeaways: Empathy has four learnable parts
Feeling with someone beats trying to fix them
Good listening is the foundation of connection
reflect: When you're hurting, do you want advice or someone to listen?

title: From Numbness to Feeling: Understanding True Emotional Maturity
desc: Emotional maturity isn't controlling your feelings, it's letting yourself feel them. On numbness, anxiety, body acceptance, and identity.
summary: On the drive to her first spa day, Hallie shares an idea from 101 Essays That Will Change the Way You Think: emotional maturity depends on how fully you let yourself feel, not how well you control your feelings.

She talks about what numbness really is, anxiety as resistance to emotion, how suppressed feelings show up in the body, body acceptance after pregnancy, and how the people who know your patterns can be both your support and your mirror. She also shares an emotional conversation with her sister that led to a breakthrough.
takeaways: Feeling fully is a sign of maturity, not weakness
Numbness is often protection
Suppressed emotions show up in the body
The people closest to us can show us our patterns
reflect: What feeling have you been numbing instead of feeling?

title: From Anger to Awareness: Managing Emotions in Unexpected Moments
desc: Is anger sometimes sadness in disguise? EQ vs SQ, emotional triggers, unprocessed grief, and three takeaways for responding instead of reacting.
summary: Is anger sometimes sadness in disguise? Hallie explains the difference between emotional intelligence and social intelligence and how building one strengthens the other.

She then works through a listener's story about a surprise family dinner where an unexpected guest stirred up grief that had never been processed. Her three takeaways: your reactions aren't always the truth, old pain shows up in new moments, and asking what you're avoiding is the first step toward emotional intelligence.

title: Walk and Reflect: Learning Emotional Intelligence on a Breezy Sunday
desc: On a Sunday walk, Hallie starts a series on emotional intelligence: naming your feelings, active listening, and responding instead of reacting.
summary: On a breezy Sunday walk, Hallie starts a series on emotional intelligence, inspired by 101 Essays That Will Change the Way You Think, and asks why so few of us were ever taught how to actually feel our emotions.
She covers identifying and naming emotions, active listening, communication in relationships, social awareness, and choosing to respond instead of react.
takeaways: Most of us were never taught how to feel
Naming an emotion takes away some of its power
Responding instead of reacting is a choice you can practice
reflect: What emotion is hardest for you to name when it's happening?

title: Real Talk, Real Healing: The First Episode
desc: The very first episode: honest conversation about breakup regret, decisions made in anger, forgiving yourself, and moving forward.
summary: Where it all started. In the first episode of the podcast, then called My Sister's Closet, Hallie introduces the show as a place for honest advice and conversations that help you grow.

She reacts to a Reddit post about regretting a breakup, looking at what went wrong, what could have happened instead, and how to move forward after a decision made in anger. Topics include relationship regret, forgiving yourself, and communicating better next time.
takeaways: Decisions made in anger often need a second look
Forgiving yourself is part of moving on
Better communication starts with slowing down
reflect: Is there a decision you made in anger that you need to forgive yourself for?
